title: A Promise for the Postcard
premise: Theo Hartwell, a widowed single father keeping the town's only bookshop afloat, agrees to pose as the date of returning local hero Dr. Amara Voss at her family's reunion, where her powerful father expects her to announce an engagement to a business ally. What begins as a transactional lie deepens into real love even as Amara discovers her father's empire is built on the land grab that ruined Theo's late wife's family. When Theo must choose between a career-saving contract tied to the Voss name and exposing the truth that could destroy Amara's family and his own livelihood, he chooses truth. In the end, Amara walks away from her inheritance, the bookshop survives as a community co-op, and the two build the family neither thought they'd have.
about_author: Cyrus Joubert is the pen name of a former small-town bookseller who spent a decade watching love stories unfold between the shelves before writing his own. He lives in a coastal village where every reunion, rumor, and second chance eventually finds its way to him.

chapters.title: The Last Bookshop on Harbor Street
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. A rainy Tuesday in the struggling bookshop introduces Theo, his eight-year-old daughter Junie, and the eviction notice tucked inside a returned novel. The emotional beat is quiet desperation masked by routine warmth.

chapters.title: A Stranger Buys Poetry
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. Back in town for her father's sixtieth-birthday reunion, Amara wanders into the shop she loved as a girl and buys a poetry collection she once abandoned there. She and Theo recognize each other from high school; the beat is tentative recognition and old ache.

chapters.title: Invitations and Ultimatums
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. At the Voss estate, her father Edmund announces she'll arrive at the reunion gala engaged to investor Marcus Hale or lose her seat on the family foundation board. The beat is gilded pressure and quiet rebellion.

chapters.title: An Offer Between the Shelves
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Amara returns to the bookshop and, half-joking, asks Theo to be her fake boyfriend for the weekend of family events. He refuses — until she mentions the foundation funds the literacy program keeping his lease alive. The beat is reluctant bargain.

chapters.title: Rules of Engagement
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Over coffee, they draft terms: no real feelings, no questions about the past, one weekend only. Junie, eavesdropping, is delighted by 'Miss Amara.' The beat is playful contract-making laced with mutual wariness.

chapters.title: The Rehearsal Dinner
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo meets the formidable Voss clan, survives Edmund's probing questions, and watches Marcus claim Amara's arm. But a shared glance across the table feels dangerously unscripted. The beat is performance tipping toward authenticity.

chapters.title: What the Tide Brought Back
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. A morning beach walk with Theo cracks open their shared history: the summer they almost kissed at seventeen, and why she left town without goodbye. The beat is confession and unfinished grief.

chapters.title: Junie's Field Trip
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Amara volunteers to chaperone Junie's class trip and is effortlessly folded into their small family — pancakes, scraped knees, bedtime stories. Theo watches his daughter adore her and panics quietly. The beat is found family forming too fast.

chapters.title: The Gala
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. At the reunion gala, the fake engagement goes public; Edmund toasts them while Marcus seethes. Dancing with Theo, Amara forgets the audience exists. The beat is the lie becoming indistinguishable from want.

chapters.title: Dessert and the First Truth
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. After the gala, over leftover dessert in the closed bookshop, they kiss for real and agree — wordlessly — that the rules are broken. The beat is surrender, sweet and terrified.

chapters.title: The Contract
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. A developer offers Theo a lucrative deal: sell the bookshop building to a Voss-affiliated project, securing Junie's future and his retirement. The catch: sign within two weeks and keep quiet about the project's origins. The beat is temptation with teeth.

chapters.title: Ledgers and Land
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. Reviewing foundation files, Amara finds evidence her father's fortune began with the forced buyout of the Hartwell-adjacent harbor properties twenty years ago — including the building that ruined her late mother's best friend, Theo's wife's family. The beat is dawning horror.

chapters.title: Two Weeks
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Both carry secrets now: Theo knows what the contract costs others; Amara knows what the Voss name cost Theo. Their romance deepens in stolen hours while each postpones confession. The beat is intimacy shadowed by dread.

chapters.title: Marcus Makes His Move
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. Marcus, suspicious of the fake engagement, threatens to expose it to Edmund unless Amara ends things and honors the original arrangement. The beat is blackmail tightening the screws.

chapters.title: The Eviction Clause
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo learns the developer deal will demolish three neighboring businesses — friends of Junie's, fixtures of the town. Signing saves his shop and betrays everyone else. The beat is the price of survival made concrete.

chapters.title: Confessions at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. On the beach where they first told truths, both confess everything in the same breath — the contract, the ledgers, the lies. Anger flares, then something steadier: a pact to face Edmund together. The beat is rupture becoming alliance.

chapters.title: Edmund's Study
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. Amara confronts her father privately; he admits the land grab and offers her the same bargain he offered everyone: complicity in exchange for belonging. The beat is power's corruption laid bare, and a daughter refusing it.

chapters.title: The Board Meeting
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo publicly declines the contract at the foundation board meeting, presenting the old deeds and naming the families harmed. Edmund retaliates instantly: the literacy funding is pulled and the lease terminated. The beat is sacrifice with immediate cost.

chapters.title: Empty Shelves
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Packing the bookshop with Junie, Theo hits his lowest point — he chose right and lost everything anyway. Amara arrives not with comfort but with a plan. The beat is grief met by resolve.

chapters.title: The Town That Read Together
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. Amara resigns from the foundation, forfeits her inheritance, and rallies the town: a community-owned bookshop co-op, funded by small pledges from hundreds of neighbors. Marcus, exposed as Edmund's enforcer, withdraws. The beat is collective rescue.

chapters.title: A Promise Kept Twice
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Edmund, isolated and diminished, makes no apology but releases the harbor properties' claims. Theo reopens the shop under new ownership, and finds Amara waiting with the poetry collection from chapter two — finally finished, finally given. The beat is earned homecoming.

chapters.title: Postcard from Harbor Street
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, closing on Junie. One year later: the co-op thrives, Junie has two parents' worth of Sunday pancakes, and a postcard arrives — Amara's handwriting, promising she's on the last ferry home. The beat is second chances, kept.
